# Stripe Checkout Friction Log

**Olga Kostina** | olgakostina3125@gmail.com | September 2026

**Live demo: https://stripe-test-rosy.vercel.app/**

A working Stripe Checkout subscription integration for Llama Inc., in test mode. Test cards and SEPA IBANs are printed on the page:

- `4242 4242 4242 4242` — instant success
- `AT32 1904 3002 3547 3204` — SEPA, resolves after ~3 minutes, so you can see the asynchronous "processing" state become confirmed
- The **Live subscriptions** panel reads from the Stripe API on each refresh, so the subscription you create appears there with its status, amount and current billing cycle

---

## Context

*Which user archetype I was channeling, what I was trying to achieve, and why I went through this flow.*

I was channeling the founder of Llama Inc., a digital travel assistant. My key business goal is selling my service. I am interested in reliable payments, fast go-live and good user experience. I want to relay the complexity to Stripe and focus on my business.

As Olga, my goal was to build a payment flow, test edge cases and observe my journey.

I split the goal into deliverables (with time spent):

- Shell UI and backend (1.5h)
- Webhooks (0.5h)
- Payment processing, sync and async (1h)

After configuring webhooks I had to choose between a hosted page, an embedded page and Elements. I opted for the hosted page for speed. I compromised on potential conversion impact, but gained speed in getting to a working prototype.

I used Claude Code to guide the implementation, Vercel to host the front end and back end, and Stripe's hosted Checkout page for payments. The integration code is mine in the sense that I directed the design, chose the flows to build and debugged them; I have noted below where I leaned on AI to interpret Stripe's behaviour.

---

## Key findings

### What was good

- The platform leads directly to the Docs.
- Onboarding guidance is very helpful.
- Impressive that companies can have their own domain in the URLs of payment links.
- I liked that Workbench forces developers to create webhook endpoints for both snapshot and thin payload structures — this is future-proofing the integration.
- Enabling a hosted page was very easy.
- Incredible that the transaction overview in the dashboard shows me a shopper is pending completing a payment on redirect from iDEAL.

### What could be improved

Severity: 🔴 broke or reversed my work · 🟠 cost me time and round trips · 🟡 friction, no time lost

**Theme 1 — The sandbox makes account activation look mandatory when it isn't**

- 🟠 The onboarding flow makes you think that account activation is necessary in order to test payments, which introduces a delay for a developer. I had to go to the docs to confirm that I do not need to activate my account to test.
- 🟡 Account activation in NL is available only in Dutch while the rest of the UI is in English, and the page cannot be auto-translated.

**Theme 2 — Guidance is not shaped to the integration I am building** *(this is where I lost the most time)*

- 🟠 The onboarding guide directed me to create a Payment Link while I thought I was creating a hosted payment page. After setting up the link I realised it is not a hosted payment page but a hosted payment link — the wrong product. It cannot be used dynamically to charge shoppers.
- 🟠 The onboarding guide and the docs lead to two different product setup UIs.
- 🟠 In Workbench it is impossible to know which events my integration type needs. I had to edit the webhook events twice — I guessed Billing and Checkout, did not know I needed Customer, and later found I had missed Invoice. Very frustrating.
- 🟡 It was not clear why I need snapshot vs thin payloads, or how the events I selected affect that choice.
- 🔴 The dashboard's product page makes the Product ID far more visible than the Price ID, which needs an extra click, so I mistook it for the parameter to set up a session. My first deployment failed with `No such price: 'prod_VBIuPzyV1mStNN'`.

**Theme 3 — Local payment methods are off by default and hard to find**

- 🟠 A page with hosted payments was quick to go live, and Klarna and cards were readily available, but iDEAL was not enabled by default. Even though I did not activate my account or register my business in NL, I am using a public IP address from the Netherlands.
- 🟠 It was very hard to find where I can enable iDEAL. It is not in the sidebar, I could not find Settings, and I had to go through the search bar.

**Minor**

- 🟡 Product description is a manual text fill-in: it does not autocorrect, and there is no auto-suggested text.

---

## Recommendations

Two improvements I would prioritise, and one I considered and deliberately ranked lower.

### 1. Guide developers to the webhook events their use case needs

**What it looks like for the user.** In the webhook set-up flow, ask what I am building — subscriptions, one-off payments, marketplace. If I say subscriptions, preselect the event categories that use case actually needs (customer, billing, checkout, invoice) and show me in one line why each one is there. I can still add or remove anything.

**Rationale.** Different use cases need non-obvious event categories, and developers don't know which ones ahead of time. I edited my events twice and still missed the invoice events until I went back to the docs. Each miss is a round trip to Workbench at exactly the moment a developer is trying to see their first successful payment, so this is cheap time to give back.

**Consideration.** One integration can serve several use cases at once, so this should preselect and explain, never restrict.

### 2. Make the Product ID / Price ID mismatch self-correcting

**What it looks like for the user — API.** When I passed a Product ID into `line_items[0].price`, Stripe returned:

```
No such price: 'prod_VBIuPzyV1mStNN'
```

The prefix already tells Stripe exactly what I did wrong. The error could instead say:

```
No such price: 'prod_VBIuPzyV1mStNN'. This is a Product ID, and a Price ID is
expected here. The default price for this product is 'price_...'.
```

**What it looks like for the user — Dashboard.** Show the Price ID at the same level of visibility as the Product ID on the product page, with a copy button, since the Price ID is the one that goes into the integration.

**Rationale.** Every subscription integration passes a Price ID, and creating the session is one of the first API calls a developer makes. Today the error is a dead end that sends you back into the dashboard to hunt for an ID that is deliberately less prominent than the wrong one. This is a change to error copy and to visual hierarchy, not new infrastructure, and it removes a failed deployment from the first-run experience.

### Considered, ranked lower: enable local payment methods for the markets I intend to sell into

**What it looks like for the user.** During Checkout set-up, ask which markets I plan to sell into and enable the relevant local methods in test mode in one click, so my test checkout looks like my real one — iDEAL for the Netherlands, for example.

**Why I didn't lead with it.** My first instinct was to infer this from the developer's IP address, but that doesn't hold up: IPs are unreliable (VPNs, distributed teams), and payment method availability depends on the merchant's country, entity and regulatory context rather than on where the developer happens to be sitting. Asking about intended markets is the version that survives. I ranked it third because the surface already exists in payment method settings, so this is mostly a discoverability problem, and it affects a narrower group — developers selling into markets with a dominant local method — than the first two.

| **Accepting payments** | |
| ![][image17] ![][image18] | Making a plan with Claude to implement payments [as a hosted page](https://docs.stripe.com/payments/accept-a-payment?payment-ui=checkout&ui=stripe-hosted#redirect-customers). I chose the hosted page and planned the implementation steps and the shopper experience. My first deployment failed because I used the Product ID instead of the Price ID in [`line_items[0].price`](https://docs.stripe.com/api/checkout/sessions/create#create_checkout_session-line_items-price). It turns out the success page was correct: iDEAL gives [immediate notification](https://docs.stripe.com/payments/ideal) of success or failure, so the first subscription payment confirms before the redirect back, and it is the [renewals that run off the SEPA Direct Debit mandate](https://docs.stripe.com/billing/subscriptions/ideal) iDEAL sets up. I used Claude to form this hypothesis and then confirmed it in the docs. 🟡 |

---

## What I did not test

Within the time box I stayed on the path from zero to a first live subscription, so this log does not cover: the customer billing portal, upgrades, downgrades and proration, renewals and dunning after a failed invoice, tax, wallets (Apple Pay and Google Pay), 3DS on renewals, or the embedded Checkout and Elements integration paths.
